notes:
Account summary: PeakRamp operates omnichannel support (voice/chat/email) for large retail + fintech customers; ~1,700 contact center agents across NA/EU. Primary objective: add LLM-powered agent assist + automated summarization but must be resilient during heavy seasonal spikes and incident bursts (Black Friday / product launches).

Key pain: recent holiday surge (Nov 2024) caused long queue backpressure and several downstream timeouts; ops wants graceful degradation and predictable per-token economics under 3-5x baseline traffic. They explicitly called out need for reliable tool-calling (ticket updates, CRM writes) without duplicate actions during retries.

Quote from Priya Shah (Head of Ops): "We need predictable latency during the 3-hour holiday spike window — can't have timeouts that cascade into missed SLAs. If the AI layer trips, fall back to safe cached replies and surface actions to agents."

Technical requirements (explicit):
- 95th pctl generation latency target: <=200ms under 2x baseline; acceptable graceful-degradation beyond that window.
- Throughput: support 5x baseline RPS in synthetic spikes for POC (target 10k concurrent short chats).
- Tool-calling guarantees: exactly-once semantics for CRM writes (idempotency tokens), audit trail.
- Model preferences: open to Llama-family quantized variants for cost, but must support verified fallbacks (smaller / cheaper models) per routing policy.
- Cost sensitivity: strong — needs predictable unit economics and batching/cache suggestions from Redwood Optimize.

POC plan: 2-week program to validate spike handling + functional correctness. Milestones:
- Week 0: baseline measurements + map common prompt shapes.
- Week 1: run synthetic 3x and 5x RPS with real chat transcripts (anonymized) to test autoscale and routing.
- Week 2: test graceful degradation (cache-only mode), measure 95/99 latency, end-to-end tool-calling idempotency, finalize SLA language.

Security/compliance: SSO/SAML mandatory, full audit logging, KMS integration for key management, data residency controls for EU customers. Legal flagged retention and residency clauses as blockers; security team requested Redwood's encryption at rest and in transit docs.

Operational asks: warm model pools for VIP clients, faster autoscale ramp (sub-60s ideally), pre-warming hooks during known peaks, circuit-breaker thresholds exposed to ops. Also want token-level cost dashboard per route.

Commercial notes: Preferred procurement: Dedicated capacity + Private control plane for regulated customers. Target ARR band shared with Finance ($300k-$1M). Forecast close aimed for 2026-06 pending successful POC and legal signoff.
